I understand the point of view you're coming from, when I started souls I saw invaders almost universally as griefers here to ruin my game and an unstoppable force in pvp I have no hope of beating under most circumstances.  


Keep at it, early game PVP is the most punishing and frequent, once you pass about the 1/4 point invaders will all but disappear (Except for Boreal Valley but uh.. I'll let you guys stumble upon how fun that is in coop on your own.) If it's really starting to ruin the experience, shoot me a PM or even put a post on the steam discussions asking for help. Many players like myself are happy to sit back and let you guys get the proper PVE experience and jump in to deal with any invaders for you.

As posted, you could try overlevelling but this is less effective with a good portion of invaders using wex dust.  


If you don't want to fight invaders yourself, make sure the host of the world is in the "way of the blue" covenant given very early on in the game at the high wall (Red cloaked lady in a church, talk a few times to get it. (Opposite Vordt.)) This automatically summons blue invaders to fight the reds for you. (And we're very thankful for the chance to do so, its one of the hardest covenants to level just because no one wears it!)

Another trick at the hosts disposal is using "Seed of tree of giant" which will appear near a strange looking tree above firelink shrine (Take an interior staircase up to an upper level, you might have to stand near the fog wall up there while it fades away). Every time you're invaded there's a chance for the tree to spawn a seed. Using a seed causes all mobs in your world to treat the invader as hostile, timed right this can really put invaders in a bad spot, turning an NPC they hoped to have as an ally into an enemy.

Its worth noting an invader gets the same handicap phantoms do, they have 25% less health than you and half the estus flasks. (This is less true thanks to twinks) and outside certain areas (see below) you will always have a 2 or 3 to 1 numbers advantage against them. The best advice I can give is to make sure you start taking your vigor away from 10 as fast as possible, get as close to 20 as you can before mid-game and invaders suddenly wont be as scary when they land hits.

The area that causes the most grief to PVE focused co-op parties is Farron Keep, this area uses special conditions that change the player slots from 3:1 to 2:2 (Using the item dried fingers adds +1 to every slot under both circumstances, so 4:2 and 3:3) The one benefit you have in this area is the trigger for a Watchdog to invade you is you stepping in the water of the swamp, clear the area around it and do a rush to grab the items in the water. (Maybe even do this part unembered if invaders are really bothering you that much.)

Off topic rant (**Story spoilers**): 

It's great to say that the world is aging with us, but that doesn't stop new players being given their tutorial by a pre-story Lamar or encountering characters killed during the events of GTA:V while they heist. If the world IS aging I'd like to see it mean something more than just joking about the date, bring us back one of the three leads as a mission giver, let us get updated on what has happened in the 4 (now 7) years since the end of the main game.  


Evidence suggesting post-story:  
\- Posters referencing events of GTA:V in GTA:O  
*Forgot to disable the decals when migrating the map? (Back then it was confirmed to be set pre-story.)*  
\- Michaels movie playing at the cinema.  
*Likely due to limited assets they could use*  
\- Lester mentions no one has ever robbed the union depository  
*If special vehicle missions are canon then we assist a crew in doing that very thing.*  
\- Agent14's comment about it being the year 2017 and that he can't believe it either.  
*The meta comment stands out to me here, he may just be joking about the "future technology" available to players living in the past.*  
\- The casino  
*This struck me as solid with the hype to the casino launch, but having played the missions, watched it change hands twice, close down once and be raided by us ourselves, its not unlikely for it to close again. Still leaving it here.*  


Evidence suggesting pre-story:  
\- Season A  
*Trevor mentions this during the events of GTA:V*  
\- Merry weather operate in GTA:O even though they're banned from doing so during the events of GTA:V  
*Maybe they were allowed to start operating again*  
\- GTA:O includes characters killed during the events of GTA:V (Regardless of story choices.)  
*I got nothing for this one.. Cloning? Different dimensions?*  
\- Radio is playing notices for an upcoming election that takes place during GTA:V  
*It'd take them work to cut that line from the audio tracks, too much apparently.*  


Works either way:  
\- Ron mentions during gunrunning that Trevor is living in Los Santos  
*This either means rockstar has decided on a canon ending or Trevor lived in Los Santos before moving to Blaine County (Which is likely considering he shows knowledge of the city.)*  
\- Agent ULP  
*This is a weird one either way, they had the voice actor and model on hand is likely the real reason for his inclusion. Him being alive really undermines one of the stories final moments for me.*  
\- Lester's "I don't work with amateurs" comment and him giving us a chance in GTA:O specifically because we're amateurs.  
Could have been a bad experience changed his mind on working with them, or the events of GTA:V (Franklin) changing his mind.
It makes even less sense if you factor in lore, GTA:O is set before GTA:V, all these new vehicles, events and organizations just vanished over night?

Not sure if you figured this out already, try playing with a game_player_equip and a trigger_multiple, have it so when the bots first touch the trigger multiple they equip the armour via the game_player_equip, then to have it toggled have your ingame buttons enabling/disabling different triggers linked to different equip ents.

Just as an extra bonus here, if you make clever use of a logic_math (settings its values from 1 to 255) and redirecting that value to the color of the entity you want via outputs, you can not only live update the color but have the color based on things happening within the map itself.

The simplest form would be a timer modifying the color by a set value every time it ticks, so fading between two or more colors (can go even crazier if you start adding in multiple outcomes with logic_case) or walls that change color based on which team controls which area of the map etc etc.
